quest.title: A Centuries-Long Dream
quest.description: The light novel is a great hit. It has successfully outshone "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits." Now, it is time to catch the spirit behind it.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x525, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

talks.objective: Go to the summoning ritual site

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Miko, what is this place?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: The ideal spot for a little meet-and-greet with a certain elusive author. This is the place where we are most likely to succeed in summoning the spirit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? But it feels so eerie here...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hehe, that seems rather fitting, considering that we are dealing with the spirits of the deceased here.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: What are you so afraid of, honestly? We're finally about to meet the true author of "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits." Aren't you excited?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's heart is pounding, but Paimon's pretty sure it's not because of excitement!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hahaha. Come on, in we go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Wait up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #*whimpering* Paimon's scared... {NICKNAME}, stay close by, okay? Don't leave Paimon all alone...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What a weird painting... Miko, do you know what it's supposed to show?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hmm... Probably a scene from ancient Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's a good piece of artwork and all, but it's also kinda eerie... so it's a bit scary.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Looks like the artist signed their name... Umm... "Rakusai"? Hmm, it's not very clear.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Let's go inside and take a look.

talks.objective: Collect clues concerning the summoning ritual
Complete preparations for the summoning ritual

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Oh, you beat me to it. Looks like your brain is intact.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: So, your first possession, hmm? What was it like?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe, good. Saves me from having to explain everything again.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hearing Urakusai admit defeat has put me in the most wonderful mood. In return, it's only fair that we make sure to deliver on what they're all hoping for.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Yes. Though they only represent a tiny proportion of the memories in the Ley Lines, it will still be quite a sight to behold when the time comes.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Since you've come this far, why don't you do one last thing for me, hmm? I'll need your help with the ritual.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You cannot be serious, Miko! After all that, you still have more errands for us?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph, you guys teamed up to scare Paimon just now. If you think Paimon's gonna do anything you ask for, think again!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Aw, come on, I'm really only asking you to finish what you started. Besides... your paychecks are still in my hands. Heh, heh, heh.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's paycheck!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: My paycheck!!!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, well there's no way out now... We're in too deep.

choices.text: I just couldn't get in on the conversation myself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, this place is huge! Hey, is that... a mirror?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's a really weird-looking stool as well. Wonder what it's for?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Ah, I see. Heh, this setup is quite handy. Saves me a lot of work.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Alright, go and take a look around. There should be a mechanism somewhere that makes the whole room move.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, it's that painting we just saw! It's turning this way, along with the whole wall!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's getting eerier and scarier! Wh—What is this place!?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Okay. Next, I will show you a secret kitsune spell. This painting is a "swift summoning medium," which means I'll be able to skip many of the more tedious steps.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: The murky mirror reflects the view of Inazuma in a bygone age. Spirits stirred by the sight of the past will be easily drawn to it.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: You're up next, little one. Come on, sit yourself down here.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Yes, the whole point of a summoning ritual is for a dead person's spirit to possess a living person's body.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: You saw what happened to that oni samurai's spirit. After leaving the host's body, he was only able to maintain his form for a very short time before disappearing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Are we positive that summoning a spirit to possess {NICKNAME} isn't gonna have any lasting negative consequences?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Aw, you really care about the little one quite a lot, don't you? Hm, I'm a little jealous. I wish my friends were caring like that.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Anyway, are you scared, little friend? Don't you worry, now, it'll be over soon. Just think of it like having a dream.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What do I need to do?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Sit on the chair, stare at the painting, and relax your body and mind. But try and be natural, there's really no need to be nervous.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #It's like {NICKNAME}'s sitting inside the painting.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? Is Paimon seeing things? Did the painting just move!?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Recite the incantation in your heart, little one. Also, you'll need to have some intense thoughts going through your head — a wish, for example.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Now, what kind of wish do we think it would take to summon forth the author of "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits"? Anyone?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Umm... probably something to do with writing?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Very good! The wish needs to be heartfelt, though, so let me help add a little realism to the equation:

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: "The book is selling exceptionally well, Traveler, but we're going to need an outline for chapter four as soon as humanly possible. When is the earliest that you can turn it in by?"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The painting is moving again! What the—
Haw-haw... I never thought the day would come when I'd be summoned using my own ritual! Getting a taste of my own medicine...
What have we here? Another budding writer? What's come over you all, why is everyone wishing for help with their writing? Are novels so popular in this day and age?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We got you! So, you were the one who wrote "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What are you trying to do, hmm? Why'd you put that summoning incantation in the book, huh? What's your game here?
Huh? What's this?
Oh, ho-ho, I see... No wonder this felt so familiar. I've walked right into your trap, haven't I.

You ask me what my game is here? Well of course... it was to use this incantation as a means for all the souls of the departed youkai to make their glorious return to the world and plunge all of Inazuma into a brutal, bloody war!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? Paimon knew it! You had an evil plan all along!
Oh, did you now? Then how naive of you to let me possess this body so easily!
#I sense... Yes, great power within {F#her}{M#him}...
Good... good! With this power, no one shall be able to stand in my way!
Mwuhahahahahaha!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Wake up, {NICKNAME}! Quick, wake up! We gotta stop him!
#It is futile... you shall never wake {F#her}{M#him} again! This body now belongs to me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Come on, wake up! Don't let him take your mind!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Miko! Think of something! Miko! Miko!!!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Pfff...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Bahahahaha...
Hahahaha...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're laughing!?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Ahahahahahaha, oh, Urakusai, you haven't changed a bit. You caught on so quickly. Too perfect.

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: Haw-haw, well, you made the face enough times that I couldn't exactly miss the hint. This is what you were going for, yes? Never one to stand on the sidelines of a good spectacle, are you? Always got to dive in and fan the flames... Ah, you mischievous little kitsune, you...

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: Look what you've done to this little flying one here. Aw, poor thing's scared witless.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Pfft, you were having plenty of fun playing the bad guy a moment ago. Now you're trying blame it all on me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Urakusai? Miko, you guys know each other?

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: Yes, we do! Of course we do.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe, allow me to formally introduce the author of "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits," Urakusai.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: No, wait. To be more accurate, it's Urakusai's memory.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Memory? But... isn't he a spirit?

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: Ah, spirits, memories... they're just different words to describe the same thing. Something that comes from the Ley Lines.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Do you remember that recent incident when the rifthounds were gnawing at the Sacred Sakura's roots?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: You witnessed human memories leaking from the Ley Lines, didn't you? Well, since there are human memories, of course there are going to be youkai memories, too.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: In life, youkai possess supernatural powers, and even when they are a shadow of their former selves from a bygone era, they still have the ability to control whether they are visible or not.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Typically, youkai memories survive longer in the world than those of humans.

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: Indeed, indeed. I was wandering around the Sacred Sakura's roots, when I suddenly heard someone yelling "Please, someone, anyone! Help me write a truly amazing novel!"

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: It piqued my curiosity, so I popped inside his body and wrote a novel for him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's how it happened... But why did you include a summoning incantation in the novel?

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: Oh, little one... not to toot my own horn here, but when I was alive, I wasn't just another kitsune, no. I was a mighty and powerful Daiyouko. The memories of other youkai can't possess human bodies at will like I can.

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: But with this incantation, they can go one last little joyride in the world for a couple of days. Anything they're still itching to do, they can go and get it done!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, but... but...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: She's trying to say that all the commotion this causes is likely to be a great disturbance to the humans.

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: Disturbance? Haw-haw, I guess you mean that we might leave them with some broken dreams after we leave, hmm? Oh, yes, and they might have a fever, or whatever.

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: But you know, I actually think that the most admirable thing about human beings is the way that they go out and shape their fate with their own two hands, given that they're not born blessed with the same powers that we enjoy.

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: As for those who would rather draw on external power than seek to improve themselves, it's quite right that they learn their lesson eventually.

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: So when you think about it, we're actually doing the humans a big favor. Miko, you agree, don't you?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe, yes, that's what I thought, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright then... You've finally convinced Paimon, you guys were right.

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: What are you scared of, little one? Don't be deceived by her day-to-day antics. Miko is actually one of the most powerful youkai out there.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Not only that, Urakusai, but my latest work has beaten that book you wrote, "A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits," to become the most popular in Inazuma.

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: Hmph, of course. You were never one to make extra work for yourself where you can help it, and yet you went to all these lengths to find my painting room and even took the trouble to summon me... I knew you must have some ulterior motive!

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: You were always the one to pick a quarrel with me when we all used to gather around and share stories.

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: Alright, alright. You win, I lose. Happy now?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Ha! I finally get to hear you say it, centuries later. Oh, I must say it feels good.

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: Mmm... I remember when you were just a little girl, always hanging off my shoulders. A few hundred years later, and you're all grown up.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Urakusai, how much time do you have left?

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: Not much. That goes for all of us, actually. We've all got to go back where we came from in the end.

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: Everyone's quite content in many ways, but they still can't help but ask: "Are we ever going to have another Hyakkiyakou?"

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe, don't you worry about that, Urakusai. Arrangements are being made.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: When my bell rings, it means the moonless night is upon us.

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: Haw-haw, great, wonderful! Fantastic!

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: Miko, it's been nice catching up, but I'd better conserve my energy if I want to stick it out until then. So I'll be on my way now.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Alright. Goodbye then, Urakusai.

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: One last thing, Miko... I just want to know, have you been well all these years?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I've been great, of course. Every day is a happy one.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Especially these days. Not only do I have my light novels, but I've also met these two delightfully nosy outlanders.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: And even Ei is finally starting to come to her senses. Quite a miracle, given how pig-headed she can be.

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: Oh, well great! That's fantastic!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Urakusai, you'd be right at home in this era.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: A great storyteller and artist like yourself would be the Yae Publishing House's ace in the hole. And I would personally be hounding you over your next installment.

response.speaker: Urakusai
response.text: Hehe, hahahaha...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He disappeared...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Are you awake, {NICKNAME}? How are you feeling?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Are you all there? Here, like last time, repeat after me—
